one_line_contribution: A measurement protocol and a single headline number (the substitution ratio S) for how much of a procedural-experience memory bank's reported benefit survives once a reflective prompt optimizer has been trained on exactly the same episodes, plus a frozen offline-compiled-bank arm (C/M2) testing whether per-instance retrieval buys anything over compiling the bank once.
closest_prior_work: Two lines the proposal never cites. (1) The instruction-vs-demonstration ablations inside the prompt-optimization literature itself (MIPROv2, Opsahl-Ong et al., arXiv 2406.11695): DSPy-family work already treats instructions and demonstrations as two slots of one prompt and already measures how much the bootstrapped-demo slot adds on top of an optimized instruction at matched training data. A retrieved ExpeL bank is a demo selector with a distillation step in front of it - the proposal concedes exactly this by adding arm R (M3) and predicting in Falsifiable Prediction 7 that M1 beats M3 by <3 points. If prediction 7 holds, the paper reduces to 'dynamic few-shot demonstrations add little on top of an optimized instruction', which is a known DSPy-era result restated on agent benchmarks. (2) The compile-experience-into-one-context line - Dynamic Cheatsheet (arXiv 2504.07952) and Agentic Context Engineering / ACE (arXiv 2510.04618) - which build a cumulative static context from past episodes and benchmark it directly against GEPA. That is precisely the comparison behind the 'risky' prediction 3 (frozen compiled instruction within 2 points of live retrieval), already run as a method paper. Neither threatens the specific S estimand or the matched-training-episode constraint, but both make the framing far less new than the Related Work section claims, and their absence from the search is the novelty problem.
strongest_objection: The primary endpoint is not powered to distinguish the predicted outcome from the refutation outcome, by the proposal's own arithmetic. Measurement gives numerator SE approx 2.0 points and, from the stated McNemar MDE of 4 points at n=600, denominator SE approx 1.4 points on a gated denominator of 10. At the predicted S=0.6 (numerator 4 points over denominator 10), the delta-method SE on the ratio is about 0.20, so the 95 percent interval on S runs roughly 0.2 to 1.0 - it does not exclude 0.3, which is the exact criterion Falsifiable Prediction 1 sets for itself, and it overlaps the refutation band (S<0.3 with CI excluding 0.6) declared in REFUTATION. Risk Factor 6 already concedes S cannot be resolved better than about plus/minus 0.2, which contradicts prediction 1 rather than qualifying it. The same problem sinks prediction 3: 'I0xM2 within 2 points of I0xM1' is an equivalence claim run at an MDE of ~4 points on E1 and ~6 points on E2, with no TOST or pre-registered equivalence margin, so on ALFWorld it cannot be tested at all, and the stated rule that sub-MDE differences are reported as inconclusive converts the success case for prediction 3 into 'inconclusive' by construction. Layered on top: S is an additive-points ratio with no headroom control. If I1xM0 lands well above I0xM0 on a bounded accuracy scale, memory's remaining gain must compress mechanically, and the design has no arm that raises base accuracy by non-instruction means to show that any accuracy-matched control compresses it equally. B-dup does not fill that role - its leakage-driven gain will be far larger than the bank's 10 points and sits in a different region of the scale, so its low S is not evidence that the main S is substitution rather than ceiling. Finally, the study may never start: the >=10-point precheck gate is described as 'routinely reported by ExpeL/ReasoningBank-class systems', which overstates ExpeL's multi-hop QA deltas, and the research track's own starting position reports this very setup fixing zero items and breaking six to seven. The escape hatch - enrich the bank until it passes - is an unbounded engineering loop absent from the compute arithmetic, and it is also a selection step on a 150-instance dev split whose effect on the test-split denominator is never analyzed.
what_would_fix_it: Three concrete changes. (1) Re-power or re-parameterize the endpoint: report the residual absolute gain at I1 (a paired difference with a clean 4-point MDE) as the primary result and demote S to a derived descriptive quantity, or raise n / optimizer seeds until the delta-method SE on S is below 0.1; state prediction 1 as a bound on the residual in points, not as a CI on a ratio the design cannot resolve. Convert prediction 3 into a formal TOST with a pre-registered margin and drop it from E2, where n=274 makes 2-point equivalence untestable. (2) Add a headroom control that raises I0xM0 accuracy to I1xM0 level by non-instruction means (self-consistency, more ReAct steps, or a matched-difficulty subsample) and show memory's gain does not collapse there; without it, high S has a mundane ceiling explanation. (3) Fix the identification of the numerator by adding the zero-data frontier-authored instruction arm below, and make the per-instance token matching of C operational - a single frozen block cannot be token-matched per instance without building instance-specific truncations, which would silently reintroduce the retrieval the arm claims to delete; specify one fixed-length C matched to mean top-k=7 injection instead. Also replace or supplement B-dup with a non-compilable positive control whose content is procedural rather than near-duplicate factual leakage, since the claim is about procedural memory and the current control validates the instrument only in the episodic/factual regime.
missing_baseline: A zero-data frontier-authored instruction (call it I0-prime): the same frontier model that serves as GEPA reflector, ExpeL distiller and offline compiler is asked to rewrite the hand-written scaffold prompt from the task description alone, seeing no training episodes. Every point of I1 over I0 - and therefore the entire numerator of S - currently conflates 'instruction optimized on the same episodes that built the bank' with 'instruction written by a frontier model rather than by the authors'. I3 pads the hand-written prompt with boilerplate and so controls length only, not authorship or model provenance; the matched-information fairness constraint that the proposal calls the interpretive backbone is exactly what this omission breaks. A secondary omission: no arm shows the bank helping a frontier-authored-but-untrained instruction, so the paper cannot separate substitution from generic prompt quality.
preprint_collision: Candid but thin, and I count it against the submission. It reports no search queries, no venues, and no date window; it explicitly concedes that OpenReview 2026 was not swept; and it retracts five citations from the previous draft (ActMem, MAS-PromptBench, TERMS-Bench, MemAPO, and an LLM-agent memory-structure paper) as unverifiable. Retracting them is the right call, but it establishes that this pipeline has already produced unverifiable references once, which is a reason to discount the remaining single-source novelty argument rather than a reason to credit the check. Novelty then rests on one named near-miss (MemDelta) plus a self-reported unverified structural precedent (TERMS-Bench) that the authors say would be a precedent for the exact logical move if it exists - an unresolved collision left unresolved. More damaging, the search misses the two lines that actually collide: Dynamic Cheatsheet (arXiv 2504.07952) and Agentic Context Engineering (arXiv 2510.04618), which compile accumulated experience into a single evolving context and benchmark it against GEPA - that is prediction 3's comparison already published as a method - and the MIPROv2 instruction-vs-demonstration ablations (arXiv 2406.11695), which already isolate the marginal value of the demonstration slot on top of an optimized instruction at matched training data. A collision check that surfaces neither has not established that the substitution framing or the compilation prediction is new.
